steps.text: Whisk flour, baking powder, and salt together in a mixing bowl; rub in lard with your fingers until mixture resembles cornmeal. Add water; mix until dough comes together.
Transfer dough onto a lightly floured surface; knead for a few minutes until smooth and elastic. Divide dough into 24 equal pieces; roll each piece into a ball.

Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Roll 1 dough ball into a thin, round tortilla using a well-floured rolling pin. Place tortilla into the hot skillet; cook until bubbly and golden. Flip; continue cooking until golden on other side. Place cooked tortilla in a tortilla warmer; continue rolling and cooking with remaining dough balls.

raw_recipe.headline: Homemade Flour Tortillas
raw_recipe.description: This flour tortilla recipe uses flour, baking powder, salt, and lard to make traditional homemade tortillas that are perfect for tacos or burritos.
raw_recipe.name: Homemade Flour Tortillas

review.reviewBody: I wish I could give this recipe more stars! I've been using Tortillas I from this site and thought it was the best one I had found ... until this one came along. I love the fact that you don't have to use boiled water, and that you don't have to let it rest for 10 minutes. This was fast and easy to make. I halved the recipe and divided the dough in 8 golf-size balls and rolled out as thin as I could (about the width of a dime). It felt like I was rolling pizza dough instead. I lightly floured my rolling pin and surface when it was a bit sticky, and rolled from the center out, rotating the dough 90 degrees ever so often. I got smooth edges, but if the edges are jagged then too much lard/shortening was added. I cooked each tortilla for 10-20 seconds on the first side and a little less on the second size. The I wrapped them in a clean dishtowel and stored them in a shopping bag. THE BEST PART OF ABOUT THIS RECIPE IS THAT THE TORTILLAS ARE PLIABLE! Thanks for sharing this wonderful recipe, LaDonna!

I made these tonight and had to come here to say they were delicious! I used the exact measurements. I made two changes: I used fresh rendered pork lard from the butcher’s section of my local Mexican market (not the lard brick); I also kneaded the dough for about 5 minutes then formed the dough balls placing them in the bowl and covering the bowl with plastic, resting the dough for 40 minutes before rolling out the tortillas. This worked like a charm. My husband said they were better than store bought tortillas. **UPDATE** Once they cooled down, I refrigerated the left over tortillas overnight in a large ziplock bag. They heated up the next day on my comal just fine and were still pliable, soft and delicious!
Loved it and I disobey a clear instruction) warning*do not substitute lard with butter" I DID! It's still great
up the lard to at least a heaping quarter cup and let the dough rest an hour or two and the tortillas will be perfect. also i used a cast iron tortilla press

Great. I only had shortening so used that. Used hot water. Whipped dry ingredients and shortening in the Blendtec then through it in the kitchenaid mixer with the water to knead for five minutes and came out super smooth. Most time consuming thing was that my griddle only held three and a time but kids enjoyed flattening the dough balls. Family loved them.

Cut recipe in half for 12 tortillas. Boil water while mixing together flour, salt and baking soda with a whisk. Add 1 Tablespoon lard. Keep whisking. You want it to look like tiny peas like a pie crust. Start adding 1/4 cup hot water in middle of flour pile and keep whisking. Then another 1/4 cup water, keep whisking/ scraping , then last 1/4 cup water, keep working the water into the flour. Divide into 12 balls, rolling smoothe. Cover with plastic wrap. Then cover the bowl with a hot wet towel. With flour on each rolling pin , roll out each as thinly as you can where you can almost but not actually see through them. Heat up comal to medium. Use spray oil if needed. Cook a bit on each side. We like brown toasted marks on ours.

Great recipe! But don't do a full whole wheat flour replacement as I just tried, they end up tough in comparison to all purpose flour, which I've used for this recipe before (I always try recipes as written before modifying) and they're always perfect. Do wrap them in a dish towel and stick them in a plastic bag as you're making them. The moist heat keeps them soft. If you don't have a comal, just flip a cast iron pan over on the burner, upside down, to give you a larger surface for large flour tortillas (corn tortillas you'd make smaller and they fit inside pans well enough).

I was told by an expert that they taste Mexican. They do have a good taste but they are a little chewy. I may need more lard. Next time I need to roll the dough into balls first so my assembly line: balls, tortilla press, skillet works betters.

Simple, I used butter instead of lard and because I used just 1 cup of flour, I eyeballed the butter and it worked perfectly, it yielded 2 large ones which filled me up. A bit messy to make but a staple for my lunchbox.

We will never buy store bought flour tortillas again! 

This recipe is easy and delicious. I do substitute lard for Coconut Oil, it's amazing, and I absolutely insist on using Hot Water. It makes a huge difference in the softness! 

I do let the mix rest after the balls are formed, but that is my preference, and not necessary if Hot Water is used. 

If done correctly they reheat and are just as soft as a fresh batch, which is hard to find in most recipes. 

If you love breakfast tacos, quesadillas, or burritos... this recipe is an absolute must-try!

Very nice, light and fluffy. Far superior to store bought tortillas.

I weighed out the dough then divided that number by the number of tortillas I wished to make. Then I weighed each smaller dough ball.

Don't gather scraps or try to re-roll a botched tortilla. The dough will get overworked and you'll get a tough, chewy tortilla that won't puff up at all when you cook it.

This was my first effort making flour tortillas. I am well experienced in baking and I offer one important suggestion. When rolling the dough balls work with three at a time. in sequence flatten the first in a layer of flour and then flatten a second, Make a first rolling pin pass on #1 and flour #3 make a second rolling pass on #1 and a 1st pass on #2. Back to #1 now somewhat relaxed by the delay and make a rolling pass. I was not successful rolling my first 2 or 3 thin enough but after I applied the short rest I was able to achieve a desirable thinness without excessive pull back. The timing became such that the piece in the skillet was done by the time the next was properly rolled.

Good recipe! I ended up cutting the recipe in half for my small family. But besides that I used Bacon fat for my lard and everything turned out great. Probably some of the best homemade tortillas I've made. I'll be using this one for now on
Great recipe. Thank you
I don’t understand how people say is a good recipe. Two tablespoons of fat is not enough! I have been making tortillas for many years.
Didn't have lard, used butter instead.
Followed recipe exactly. Simple and delicious!
Love this recipe! It's my go to for making flour tortillas now! No need for store bought at all anymore.

I like this recipe for flour tortillas, I had to flour everything quite heavily to keep the raw dough from sticking . My only other recommendation would be to not overwork the dough, the more you work it , the tougher it gets to roll out thinly.
Worked great! Looks and tastes like a tortilla. Simple ingredients I had on hand.
